sla.counting_rule: The first working day is the first England and Wales working day on or after the calendar day after receipt. Cabinet Office Guide to Handling Correspondence, September 2024, paragraph 9. PDF retrieved 26 October 2026. The Guide does not define working day. This count uses the England and Wales bank-holiday calendar in working_days.py.
sla.holding_reply_note: Guide paragraph 20, retrieved 26 October 2026. A holding reply does not clear the case. This clock does not move the date, and the agent does not send a holding reply.
sla.transfer_note: Guide paragraph 21 times a transfer request (within one working day) and the receiving department's response (three working days for ministerial correspondence, five for public correspondence) from the transfer. This agent does not send a transfer, so those dates are not calculated. Paragraph 24's three-working-day contribution is also not calculated.
sla.calendar: England and Wales bank holidays, plus any extra closed dates the author passed. Scotland and Northern Ireland are not encoded.

correspondence_hub.note: The hub says departments will aim to respond within 20 working days, and that correspondence is separate from FOI, SAR, and complaints processes. Page last updated 25 September 2026 on the copy retrieved 26 October 2026.

vulnerability.note: A flag quotes words from the letter. It does not label the person, and it is not written to a case record. Immediate-risk wording needs a person before anyone else relies on the draft.
